# New-ZbxConnector

## SYNOPSIS

Creates a connector.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxConnector [[-Name] <string>] [[-Url] <string>] [-Protocol <ZabbixConnectorProtocol>] [-DataType <ZabbixConnectorDataType>] [-ItemValueType <int>] [-AuthType <ZabbixHttpAuthentication>] [-Username <string>] [-Password <SecureString>] [-Token <SecureString>] [-MaxRecords <int>] [-MaxSenders <int>] [-MaxAttempts <int>] [-AttemptInterval <string>] [-Timeout <string>] [-HttpProxy <string>] [-VerifyPeer <bool>] [-VerifyHost <bool>] [-SslCertFile <string>] [-SslKeyFile <string>] [-SslKeyPassword <SecureString>] [-Description <string>] [-Status <ZabbixConnectorStatus>] [-TagsEvalType <ZabbixConditionEvalType>] [-Tag <ZabbixConnectorTagRequest[]>] [-AdditionalProperty <Hashtable>] [-Force] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A connector streams item values or events to an external HTTP endpoint as newline-delimited JSON, for a system outside Zabbix to consume. The New-ZbxConnector cmdlet sends connector.create with one request field per parameter, then reads the new connector back with connector.get and writes it. The server requires -Name and -Url; -AdditionalProperty sets any other field by its API name and wins over a parameter. -WhatIf shows what would be created, and the command needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Create a connector

```powershell
New-ZbxConnector -Name 'Event stream' -Url 'https://events.example.com/zabbix' -DataType Events
```

Creates a connector named Event stream. The command writes the new connector, read back from the server.
